To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the semantics of a program can be defined by a partial program graph; (2) the correctness and termination of a program can also be defined by the same partial program graph; and, finally, that (3) the correctness of a program can imply its termination.

(1) the flow equivalence and correctness of programs can be described in the language of partial graphs; and that (2) the correctness and termination of recursive systems can be described in terms of the flow equivalence of partial graphs.

the relational algebra of Tarski and Riguet is a very useful tool to investigate the flow of program execution and that partial graphs are a very useful tool for the description of the single program steps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a unified theory of program semantics, correctness and flow equivalence.
the formalization of the semantics, correctness and the termination of programs and systems of programs.
the development of an algebraic theory of programs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
partial graphs are the appropriate formalism for a unified treatment of the concepts of semantics, correctness, termination, and flow equivalence.
the use of the partial graph formalism is not only a useful and powerful technique but also a very elegant and natural one.

the use of partial graphs and programs as relational algebraic tools provides a very elegant, concise and unified way to deal with the semantics, correctness and the termination of programs and systems of programs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that it is possible to use a single formal tool, the partial graphs, to describe the semantics and the correctness of programs in a natural way.
the relational algebra of Tarski and Riguet can serve as a common framework for the description and analysis of programs, their semantics, correctness and the termination of recursive procedures.
the relational approach to program semantics is not only a powerful tool to study the properties of programs but also a useful tool for the design of new programming languages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of partial graphs is a powerful tool to handle the flow of program steps and to relate it with correctness and termination.
it is possible to present a unified framework for the presentation and manipulation of these notions.
we are able to present the semantics, the correctness and termination in one formal framework.
